newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates steady, Med slips on tonnage.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates steady, Med slips on tonnage.

text.p: World crude tanker charter rates were broadly steady on Monday as the market got off to a slow start to the week. The cross Mediterranean sector, which had shown strength and activity last week was slowing and rates easier.
In the key Middle East Gulf sector traders said VLCCs were attracting similar rates to last week.
"There has been no real change it is all ticking along with with east and west (discharges) seen," said one London shipbroker.
VLCCs heading to Japan were assessed at W68-70 while 250,000 tonners heading westwards were at W55-57.

In the Mediterranean position details for several tankers have become known and recent pressure has eased. Shipping brokers said the market now looked a touch softer with below W120 achievable for mid-month loading on 80,000 tonners. An oil major looking for an aframax within the first decade might have to pay last week's levels of W120-125.
Suezmaxes looking for cross Mediterranean business were pegged at W90 for good quality tonnage while older ships would have to accept W85, dealers said.
In the North Sea benchmark 80,000 tonners were hovering around W120 for typical trips, although above and below was fixed.
West African crude continued to be drawn to the U.S with million barrel vessels paying a steady W85 for mid-late month trips.
